skill.name: code-formatter
skill.description: Automatically format code across multiple languages with opinionated configurations.
skill.summary: Automatically format code across multiple languages with opinionated configurations.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by a Markdown code fence in SKILL.md usage examples. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe runtime behavior was found in the reviewed skill text.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md lines 37-42 contain a Markdown usage example block with @code-formatter commands. This is not Ruby shell backtick execution and does not execute commands.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent formatting slows reviews and makes code harder to compare. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to format supported languages with project-aware rules.
actual_capabilities: Detects common code languages in a directory or requested path.
Checks for existing formatting configuration files before choosing defaults.
Applies language-specific formatter guidance for JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, web files, and data files.
Supports check-only and language-specific formatting requests.
Reports formatted files and style decisions after work is complete.
limitations: Requires the relevant formatter tools to be installed in the working environment.
Does not define custom formatters beyond the listed language ecosystems.
Should ask before modifying project formatting configuration files.
Must skip generated code, vendor directories, binary files, and lock files.

use_cases.title: Prepare a pull request
use_cases.description: Format changed files before review so diffs focus on behavior instead of whitespace or style drift.

use_cases.title: Standardize a mixed-language repository
use_cases.description: Apply appropriate formatter guidance across web, backend, data, and documentation files in one workflow.

use_cases.title: Audit formatting without edits
use_cases.description: Run a check-only pass to identify files that need formatting before a release or migration.

prompt_templates.title: Format the current project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for formatting the active workspace with default behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Format one directory
prompt_templates.scenario: Limit formatting to a specific source directory.

prompt_templates.title: Check formatting only
prompt_templates.scenario: Review formatting status without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Format one language
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that targets one language ecosystem and its formatter conventions.

output_examples.input: A developer asks to format a TypeScript and CSS project.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies existing Prettier settings, formats supported files, skips lock files, and summarizes the edited paths.

output_examples.input: A maintainer requests a check-only Python formatting pass.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports which Python files do not match the configured style and recommends the formatter command to run.

output_examples.input: A team asks to format a repository with Go, Markdown, and YAML files.
output_examples.output: The assistant applies the relevant formatting rules, respects existing configuration, and reports any skipped generated directories.

best_practices: Run the skill from the repository root so project configuration files are detected.
Use check-only mode before large formatting changes or release branches.
Review the final summary before committing formatting-only changes.
anti_patterns: Do not format vendor, generated, binary, or lock files.
Do not overwrite existing formatter configuration without explicit approval.
Do not mix formatting changes with unrelated feature edits in the same commit.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, CSS, HTML, JSON, YAML, and Markdown.

faq.question: Does it respect existing project settings?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to check existing formatter configuration before applying default rules.

faq.question: Can it run without changing files?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the check-only request to report formatting issues without modifying files.

faq.question: Will it edit formatter configuration files?
faq.answer: It should ask before modifying configuration files such as Prettier, EditorConfig, or Python project settings.

faq.question: Does it install formatter tools?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides formatting workflow guidance and expects required tools to exist in the environment.

faq.question: Is this useful with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is declared compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
